- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% in subsequent periods.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–3% upward bias to counteract mean reversion.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; adjust upward by 0.5–2% for short-term (1–3 day) forecasts.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly, model lags in recognizing the reversal; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 periods to avoid premature overcorrection.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate if recent sentiment is mixed or declining; apply upward bias of 1–4% based on sentiment volatility index (e.g., >0.5 standard deviation from mean).
